title: Advanced RAG Techniques: Re-ranking and Hybrid Search
summary_short: Deep dive into production RAG with re-ranking and BM25 hybrid retrieval.
summary_detail:
This tutorial covers the full RAG improvement stack: sparse retrieval (BM25) combined with dense vector search, followed by a cross-encoder re-ranker pass.

The key insight: hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms pure vector search on keyword-heavy queries (code snippets, proper nouns, version numbers) while dense search wins on semantic similarity. Combining them with a reciprocal rank fusion function captures both.

Code examples use LangChain + Qdrant + Cohere re-rank. Directly applicable to any production RAG system.

title: Building with LangGraph: Stateful Multi-Agent Workflows
summary_short: Practical guide to building stateful agent loops with LangGraph.
summary_detail:
A hands-on course segment covering LangGraph's core primitives: StateGraph, conditional edges, and checkpointing for long-running agent workflows.

The course builds a research agent that can browse, extract, reflect, and revise — all within a persistent state machine that survives interruptions and can be replayed.

Key practical implication: LangGraph's human-in-the-loop checkpointing makes it significantly easier to build agents that can pause for approval before taking destructive actions.

title: Deploying Local Models: Ollama, llama.cpp, and vLLM Compared
summary_short: Side-by-side comparison of the three main local LLM serving stacks.
summary_detail:
Eugene Yan's detailed comparison of Ollama, llama.cpp, and vLLM for local model deployment, covering throughput benchmarks, memory profiles, and API compatibility.

Findings: Ollama wins for developer experience and Apple Silicon; vLLM wins for GPU throughput at scale (2-3x); llama.cpp remains the most portable and lowest memory option.

For a personal brain / RAG use case on macOS: Ollama with Metal acceleration is the pragmatic choice — it exposes an OpenAI-compatible API and handles model management automatically.

title: Vector DB Optimization: HNSW Tuning and Index Compression
summary_short: How to tune Qdrant HNSW parameters for latency vs. recall tradeoffs.
summary_detail:
A technical deep-dive into HNSW graph parameters (m, ef_construction, ef) and how they affect recall, indexing speed, and query latency in Qdrant.

Key finding: setting ef_construction=200 and m=16 at index time is almost always worth it for collections under 10M vectors — the recall improvement is significant and the index build only takes minutes.

Bonus section on scalar quantization: enabling it on embedding vectors reduces RAM usage by 4x with less than 1% recall degradation on most datasets.

title: Production LLM Cost Management: Caching, Batching, and Routing
summary_short: Cut your LLM API spend by 60% with semantic caching and model routing.
summary_detail:
Lilian Weng's practical post on cost optimization for production LLM applications, covering three independent techniques: semantic prompt caching (cache hit = near-zero cost), request batching (2-5x throughput improvement), and intelligent model routing (GPT-4o-mini for simple tasks, full model only when needed).

Benchmark: a typical RAG-over-docs workload saw 58% cost reduction with semantic caching alone using a 0.92 cosine similarity threshold.

For this app: the same vector store (Qdrant) used for RAG retrieval can serve double duty as a semantic cache for frequently-repeated question patterns.
